Frobenius-orthogonal modes R=F_m YH_n, Q=H_m YF_n, I=F_m YF_n have covariance eigenvalues lambda_R=k(m-k)/(mn(m-1)), lambda_Q=k(n-k)/(mn(n-1)), lambda_I=k((m-1)(n-1)+k-1)/(mn(m-1)(n-1)). The positive eigenspace range equals the true affine hull, with dimensions mn-1, m(n-1), (n-1)^2 in the three boundary regimes. Each vertex has deterministic projected squared energy r_T lambda_T, so is on the ellipsoid of squared semiaxes d lambda_T. For arbitrary enclosing ellipsoid center c and shape A, averaged containment gives tr(A^-1 Sigma)+(C-c)^T A^-1(C-c)<=1, and matrix AM-GM yields det A>=d^d det Sigma, with equality only at c=C and A=d Sigma: uniqueness global, not just symmetric ansatz. Comparing modes gives squared-axis anisotropy [((m-1)(n-1)+k-1)/((n-1)(m-k))] for k<m, n/(n-m) at k=m<n, 1 at m=n=k. All last-step increase/decrease/equality integer cases follow by direct inequalities. Independently checked exact rational energies and anisotropy for 2<=m<=4, m<=n<=5, all allowed k; those finite checks do not replace the universal determinant proof.
